desc:
A server logs user sessions. Each session is a half-open time range [start, end): it is active at every integer time t with start ≤ t < end, so a session that ends at time 5 and one that starts at time 5 are never active together.

Return the earliest integer time at which at least k sessions are active at once, or -1 if that never happens. The sessions come in no particular order.

sessions = [[1, 4], [2, 6], [3, 5]], k = 2  ->  2
sessions = [[1, 4], [2, 6], [3, 5]], k = 3  ->  3
sessions = [[0, 5], [5, 9]],         k = 2  -> -1
hints: Checking every time from 0 to the maximum end is far too slow when times go up to 10<sup>9</sup>. The number of active sessions only changes at a start or an end.
Turn every session into two events: +1 at start and -1 at end. Sort the events by time and keep a running count.
At equal times process the -1 events before the +1 events (a session ending at t is not active at t). Return the time of the first +1 event after which the count reaches k.
editorial: The count of active sessions is a step function that only changes at event times. Create (start, +1) and (end, -1) for each session and sort them; tuples (time, delta) sort a -1 before a +1 at the same time, which is exactly the half-open rule.

Sweep the sorted events with a running total. The count can only increase on a +1 event, so the first time the total reaches k it happens at the time of that event, and nothing earlier can be a valid answer. If the sweep ends without reaching k, return -1. Sorting dominates: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
